units.text: WHO data for 2024 consistently report the WHO African Region at ~95% of global malaria cases, not 75%. The claim is contradicted by authoritative WHO fact-sheet and World Malaria Report spans.

citations.title: Malaria facts & statistics 2025 | Medicines for Malaria Venture

judgement.reason: The quoted WHO fact-sheet and MMV passages support ~94–95% of global malaria cases in the African Region, contradicting 75%, but no World Malaria Report span is quoted to establish consistency across WHO reports.

units.text: All cited 2024 sources give approximately 95% African Region share; the 75% figure is not supported by any evidence.

citations.title: Malaria count rose in 2023; African region still sees most cases | CIDRAP
World Malaria Report 2024: Accelerating progress and preserving the gains of the fight against malaria  | Target Malaria

judgement.reason: The passages do not state a 95% African Region share; Target Malaria gives 80% of averted cases in the African Region, and CIDRAP gives no regional share. No passage mentions a 75% figure.

units.text: The assertion that the WHO African Region accounted for 75% of global malaria cases in 2024 is false; the correct figure per WHO is about 95%.
